column1: # The mutants that survive today, per package, as a ratchet.
# package
# Measured 2026-08-16 with gremlins v0.5.0 at --timeout-coefficient 60, and
# re-measured 2026-08-17 under v0.6.0 at the same coefficient. Every count below
# is unchanged across the two, which is the answer to the question a tool bump
# always raises here and the reason none of these numbers moved with it. A count
# here is a promise that this many tests are missing, not a target: every one of
# them is a change to a line that no assertion notices. Lower it as they are
# killed, and never raise it without saying what got worse.
# Three packages, not the tree. These are the ones where a surviving mutant is a
# wrong answer somebody acts on rather than a cosmetic difference: jql builds
# every query and owns the only place a value is quoted, render writes the
# output contract, and site decides what a deployment is and resolves the names
# every command takes. The sweep costs about four minutes on a developer
# machine and, measured 2026-08-20, four minutes and one second on a
# `ubuntu-latest` runner. It is scheduled because it is slower than a test
# suite, not because a runner is slow at it: "considerably more on a runner"
# stood here unmeasured until the day somebody ran one.
# `internal/jql` went 16 to 3 on 2026-08-17. Thirteen were killed by assertions
# named in internal/jql/*_test.go; the three below are equivalent mutants, which
# is a different claim from "no test notices" and is why they are written down
# rather than left as a number somebody will try to lower.
#   date.go:367:12   `total > maxDuration-component`, boundary. The two forms
#                    differ only when the sum lands exactly on MaxInt64
#                    nanoseconds. Every unit in dateValueUnits is a whole number
#                    of minutes, so every total is a multiple of 60e9, and
#                    MaxInt64 is odd: the equality is unreachable by
#                    construction rather than untested.
#   token.go:217:10  `start+1 < len(src)`, the guard that reads two runes only
#   token.go:217:13  when two remain. Both mutants make it read one rune past
#                    the end at the end of a query. `src` is one `[]rune(query)`
#                    and every lexer takes it whole with an index, so that rune
#                    is allocator spare and reads as U+0000, which completes no
#                    two-rune operator. The mutants differ from the original
#                    only by an index-out-of-range panic when cap == len, and a
#                    test that arranged that would be asserting Go's size
#                    classes rather than this tokenizer.
# If one of those is ever killed honestly, delete its paragraph and lower the
# count in the same change. The ledger only shrinks.
# `internal/site` went 37 to 34 on 2026-08-20, and the three are not named the
# way jql's are, because a lowering owes no argument: what is written here is
# what survives, and 34 do. Three commits touched the package in the window and
# only 69ebd3a added assertions, moving the site's clock out of the change feed
# and bringing a test over every layout Jira sends.
# It was measured twice, and the second run was not a formality. A mutant can
# live in one sweep and die in the next if a test brushes the timeout, so a
# count that moved is a count to take again before a ratchet is turned on it.
# Both runs said 34 and named the *same* fifty survivors across the three
# packages, byte for byte, which is a stronger agreement than two matching
# totals would have been.
# `internal/render` went 13 to 12 on 2026-08-31, and the mutant that died is
# CONDITIONALS_NEGATION at node.go:65:11, the `value == ""` guard in
# `Node.AttrIf`. Nobody wrote a test for it. `fa6a640` put
# `root.AttrIf("project", d.Project)` and its `board` twin in xml.go, and those
# are the first calls in this package whose empty branch anything asserts: the
# XML goldens hold documents where both values are empty, so the negated guard
# emits `project=""` and `board=""` on every root element and TestGoldenOutput
# fails on collection/xml, collection-truncated/xml, and record/xml. Before
# that, the package's only caller was schema.go's `AttrIf("name", f.Name)`, and
# no test in the package noticed what that one did: the mutant lived every
# sweep from 2026-08-16 through 2026-08-24.
# Taken twice, on the rule two paragraphs up. The runner reported twelve and
# this machine reported the same twelve, byte for byte by file, line, and
# mutator, and the kill was confirmed by hand: negate node.go:65 and the three
# golden cases above go red.
# Where these numbers come from, which this file could not tell you until
# 2026-08-20 and now can.
# `mutation-weekly` failed the only two times it ran, on 2026-08-17, the second
# killed after 76 seconds with `make: *** [Makefile:421: mutate] Terminated`.
# The paragraph that first stood here read that as a runner limit. It was not.
# Both failures predate the fix, and every time here is UTC because the run log
# is: the 07:04 schedule ran before `b4169e6` (12:06), and the 12:13 dispatch
# ran *on* `b4169e6`, which is not a descendant of `50c402f`, the commit that
# bounds the address space a mutated test may claim. That commit landed at
# 13:36, 83 minutes after the dispatch it would have saved, and nobody ran the
# sweep again for three days.
# It was run on 2026-08-20 against `2a5bcf3` and succeeded, four minutes and one
# second in the sweep step, matching this file on all three packages. So the
# 34 below is corroborated by a machine that is not the one that measured it,
# and `scripts/mutate.sh`'s claim that a runner completes the sweep at 3 GiB is
# corroborated too.
# That hash was restamped on 2026-08-28: it read `2174f33` until main's history
# was rewritten to strip a trailer from fifteen commit messages, which changed
# every hash from the modernizer-gate commit (`ea8972b`, PR 96) onward without
# touching a byte of any tree. A clone taken before that date resolves the old
# hash and not this one.
# The first draft of this paragraph cited the *old* hash of that boundary
# commit, which is the defect it was written to fix, one line further down.
# The lesson is not about runners. A gate that was fixed and never re-run is
# indistinguishable from a gate that is still broken, and the distinguishing
# command took one minute. Issue 57 said exactly the right thing, "no conclusion
# about the tests follows from this run", and was closed without one.
internal/jql
